hypothesis: A structure-based ordering of tests may reveal a historical fault earlier than native lexical order or a fixed-seed random permutation at equal budgets.
defect_detection_rule: buggy unittest FAIL (assertion) and fixed PASS for the same test identifier; other errors and fixed failures do not count
source_selection: Two first non-calibration small Python unittest-based BugsInPy cases from different upstream projects; chosen from public metadata without observing test outcomes
scientific_limits: Two known patched bugs do not provide independent validation or credible estimates of generalized superiority
The common fixed-revision test file may contain a regression test crafted with bug knowledge
Only the ordering policies are outcome-blind; upstream regression test design is not blind
Test-suite order and shared process state may affect outcomes
Test outcomes measured once per revision; do not treat repeated budgets as independent bug cases
